# Port catalog

*Generated by `tools/inventory/port_inventory.py catalog` (also run by `port_inventory.py doc`) from the scan of the player's disc; do not edit by hand. The descriptions come from `tools/inventory/notes.txt` and the ports' `// orig:` comments.*

[Catalog index](README.md) · [Port inventory](../port-inventory.md)

A census of every function of the game, ported or not, of every moby class the levels list, and of the host code the port puts in place of the original's hardware, libraries and kernel. [Port inventory](../port-inventory.md) has the totals and the work left; these pages list every function one by one.

## Counts

Unique functions of the boot module and the 19 overlays: **4247**; the core libraries: **658** functions; moby classes: **1171**.

| Status | Unique functions | Bytes | Core functions | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| ported | 3930 | 3484.7 KB | 82 | the port runs it: a hand-written or generated port (`// orig:`), a registration, or the same code as such a port through the overlay maps (empty functions and those covered inline by their callers' ports count here) |
| not ported | 1 | 44 B | 0 | the game's code can reach it and the port has no port of it: the work left |
| host replacement | 92 | 16.5 KB | 0 | reached, replaced on purpose by host code (hardware, DMA, GS, kernel, the movie library): see [Host replacements](host.md) |
| host library | 0 | 0 B | 468 | a core library function the port does not port one by one: the runtime layer and the C++ libraries (`src/game/lib`) stand in for it (see [Host replacements](host.md)) |
| debug feature | 5 | 12.9 KB | 0 | reached, a development feature of the original the retail game never turns on |
| unopened menu data | 14 | 1008 B | 0 | named only by menu data that no code opens there (the title's pages carried in the levels' overlays, widgets no page lists) |
| not a function | 9 | 468 B | 0 | not a function: a data word that looks like a code pointer, a jump table's case |
| not connected | 196 | 27.6 KB | 108 | not connected: nothing reaches any copy (cut content, dead code); `(ported anyway)` when a port exists |

Among the ported: 2 empty (a bare return), 3 covered inline by their callers' ports, 0 with no port file of their own found (registered by address, a dispatch `case`, or a sky row: the port is in the file that registers it). Not connected and ported anyway: 4.

Moby classes: ported 1167, no code 4.

### Hand-written or generated

How the ported functions are ported (the `How` column): **hand**, written by hand in the repository (`src/`); **generated**, translated from the player's disc at setup by the generators of `tools/codegen` into `assets/generated/` (a hand-written registration or header declaration around it does not count); **both**, a generated body and a hand-written port of the same function (glue, an override, a level's variant). The counts are of the ported unique functions (the core's: of its ported functions; the VU microcode not included).

| Group | Hand | Generated | Both | Hand bytes | Generated bytes | Both bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| core libraries | 75 | 0 | 0 | 11.1 KB | 0 B | 0 B |
| boot module | 20 | 1 | 2 | 14.5 KB | 1.0 KB | 220 B |
| engine | 1414 | 813 | 163 | 706.8 KB | 583.7 KB | 87.1 KB |
| levels' own code | 94 | 1336 | 83 | 211.8 KB | 1154.5 KB | 724.5 KB |
| **all** | 1603 | 2150 | 248 | 944.2 KB | 1739.3 KB | 811.8 KB |

11 ported functions have no port of their own and no `How`: empty functions (a bare return) and the helpers our notes say are written into their callers' ports.

Moby classes, by how their update is ported: generated 818, hand 324, both 22, hand/generated 1.

## The columns

- **Address**: the function's Veldin address (level 0's overlay, the reference build) when Veldin has a copy; `front:0x...` (the boot module) or `Ln:0x...` (level n's overlay) otherwise. The ports carry these addresses in their `// orig:` comments.
- **Our name**: the port's function name (or the TODO_PORT stub's label). Empty: no port names it.
- **Status**: see the table above. `(empty)`, `(inline)`: how a ported one is ported; `(no port file)`: ported through a registration or a dispatch case only.
- **How**: `hand`, `generated` or `both` (see above); empty when the function is not ported.
- **Port / replaced by**: the files holding the port (the `.cpp` before its header; generated files are written by the setup into `assets/generated/`, not in the repository), or the host module that stands in.
- **Oracle batches**: the batches of `tests/oracle` that name the function's address (or that the port's comment or our note names). A batch can name an address without checking it (a caller's setup); a missing batch does not mean unproved: many ports are covered by their callers' batches.
- **Copies**: the images carrying the same instructions (`every level`, `front`: the boot module).
- **What**: our note (tools/inventory/notes.txt), else the port's `// orig:` comment, else what names it (a class row, a table).

## How to regenerate

```bash
tools/inventory/port_inventory.py scan --census <the development repository>/docs/reversing/moby_class_census.csv
tools/inventory/port_inventory.py catalog         # docs/catalog/ only
```

`port_inventory.py doc` writes both [Port inventory](../port-inventory.md) and these pages; the inventory page's runtime sections need the headless tour first (`port_inventory.py tour`, about an hour, then `scan --runtime assets/generated/inventory/tour`). The catalog does not use the tour. Without `--census` the classes' placement column is empty.
